svg.title: Occupancy slope by policy — cells gained per five-move cycle; zero is flow balance, and every fair arm is above zero
svg.desc: Occupancy slope by policy — cells gained per five-move cycle; zero is flow balance, and every fair arm is above zero. Slope is the mean over games of the least-squares slope of occupied cells against cycle index from cycle 2 onward (finding-06 section 2). The eight-tape series (findings 06/07, 8 games per arm, paired master tapes 0xa5230000-0xa5230007) is now known to be unrepresentative: finding-12 measured that those tapes favour long games, inflating fair D4's mean lifetime by 26%, so the fresh-tape series (finding-12 section 2; 128 tapes for fair D4 and planner H5 K256, 32 tapes for planner H7 K256) is the representative one and the two series are never pooled. The finding-12 cohort table prints fair D4's fresh slope as +1.481; its paired H=5 table prints the same arm as +1.4806 — both recorded, the cohort-table value is charted. Recorded but not charted (the plan's selection): clairvoyant rh-clears fresh-tape slopes +0.075 at H=7 (64 tapes) and +0.099 at H=9 (32 tapes) (finding-12 section 6), and rh-clears H9 cap-1000 slope -0.0015 over cycles 2-200 (finding-06 section 2.1). Every fair arm's slope is strictly positive and every fair game ended: 0 of 87 eight-tape fair-planner games and 0 of 160 fresh-tape fair games reached the cap. Evidence tier: development/pilot; small paired cohorts throughout. The eight-tape clairvoyant rows are privileged diagnostics (they read the hidden board), never deployable policies. Sources: docs/exploratory/finding-06-flow-ceiling.md, docs/exploratory/finding-07-fair-planning-ceiling.md, docs/exploratory/finding-12-fair-planner-ceiling-extended.md.
